text:
maria: Heads-up — dedicated canary in us-west-2 (pool-ded-42) has a sustained p99 jump of ~220ms after merge 6482 landed this morning. Rolling hold on the rollout. Any immediate ideas?

tom: @maria thanks. Do we have a quick blame path? kernel selection, batching, KV cache thrash? :eyes:

maria: Initial profiler points at kernel_hinting choosing 'merge_batch_v2' for a lot of short-seq requests. Those kernels look fine in throughput but have bad tail for batch size 1-2. Pasting the profiler snapshot we grabbed from the canary: 

```
hotspots:
  kernel_selector.select        48%
  merge_batch_v2               33%    p99 +180ms vs baseline
  continuous_autobatcher       22%    p99 +50ms
  kv_cache.eviction            5%
  io_waits                     3%
```

anita: That's surprising — merge_batch_v2 was benchmarked as better for mixed loads. Did the autotuner / hint weights change in the same PR?

devon: I ran a local repro with small_chat_seq (seq_len=16) and microbench. Results: merge_batch_v2 p99 ~210ms, merge_batch_v1 p99 ~28ms. Repro script: 

```
# repro
./bench --model tiny --seq 16 --batch 1 --kernel hint=v2
./bench --model tiny --seq 16 --batch 1 --kernel hint=v1
```

rj: @devon can you bisect to which commit in 6482 changed the hint logic? Any other touching files?

devon: Bisect points at the hint threshold tweak inside PR #6482: we lowered the hint_score cutoff so merge_batch_v2 is preferred when estimated throughput > 0.6 even for requests that are KV-heavy. With the higher prefix-KV cache hit rates in canary, estimated throughput nudged over that cutoff, routing lots of short requests to v2.

lee: So it's an interaction: cache hit rate increased -> estimator moves kernel choice -> short-single-batch requests hit a worse-tail kernel. Explains the dedicated p99 spikes (dedicated pools are heavy on short chat completions).

perf-ci: Perf CI shows the microbench 'small_chat_seq' regressed at 06:12 today after the merge — p99 +140ms, test flagged but not blocking the merge: https://ci.internal/perf/12345

amanda: @sre FYI, do we have customer impact telemetry? If SLA risk is real we need to notify and offer mitigation.

infra-bot: SRE alert: two dedicated tenants in us-west-2 reported error budget burn risk last 24h. Manual pool-level kernel override applied to pool-ded-42 at 09:15 to prefer merge_batch_v1.

maria: Confirmed. SRE applied manual override for the two affected pools. We need either a revert of the hint change or a targeted hotfix for dedicated pools.

tom: I'll open a revert PR for the hint_threshold change and re-run perf CI. If revert is risky, we can add a config override so dedicated pools bias to v1 while we iterate.

anita: Also please add a perf CI test that runs representative small-batch short-seq workloads targeted at dedicated pool profiles. This interaction between estimator and cache behavior should be covered.

rj: Action list: 1) tom open revert PR and link perf diffs 2) devon produce detailed repro and perf traces 3) anita add dedicated small-batch perf test + alerting 4) maria notify affected customers and publish rollback notes. I'll coordinate the rollback runbook.

maria: Notifying customers now. Thanks everyone. (reacted :thumbsup: by tom)
